_: Pool greetings (2.5c0): five per people and faction sheet, by standing band (faction standing 50, or the speaker's disposition 70 for a people) x time (day, night), plus the owing greeting (`owingHere`: an open Owing on the ledger of the region the player stands in, 2.10); the other bands hold only while no Owing is open there. One unconditional fallback.

entries.words: Yes? Say it.
Show your licence, citizen.
Night patrol. Which road brought you here?
Your customs mark is good, citizen.
Quiet at the border tonight, citizen.
The Wardens are watching you.
Lost, fresh meat? Gate's behind you.
At the gate at night? The archers are awake.
The east wall is yours tonight, brother.
East wall's short a spear, brother.
Step out of line again and you lose a hand.
Be welcome among the Bright-Throats, guest.
The chime-makers are working late on the frames.
Back in good time, guest. Was the water kind?
The fish is cooked, guest. There is plenty.
The chimes are off for you. Go.
Here to help, or here to count us?
Hold the lamp. I am copying.
Did the debt-roll come with you, sibling?
Bones go to the grove at dawn.
Holders pay people like you.
Your seal, colleague? I have to see it.
Do not breathe on the samples.
The survey copy came back marked, colleague.
I am busy tonight, colleague.
Every word of this goes to the Rector.
Chapter business, or just looking?
The finds are locked away for the night.
Good timing as ever, chapter-agent.
The crates are half open, agent.
You took what is catalogued. Return it.
Who let you through the gate?
No callers are taken after dark.
Your room is aired, muthsera.
The claim papers are in the press, serjo.
You will answer to the House for that.
This stretch is patrolled, civilian.
Who goes there? Your name.
The serjeant said you might pass, civilian.
Walking to the post? Come with us.
In the name of the Legion, halt.
Ward business? The clerk is inside.
The tribes still give the word on ward land, delegate.
Your seat by the window is free, delegate.
The ward count is tomorrow, delegate.
The clerk will have your name by noon.
Are you here for the tree, root-kin?
A tree-minder sits with the Hist.
Be welcome here, root-kin.
The grove edge is watched tonight, root-kin.
No shelter here for a thief.
Looking for work, or for a blade?
Night contract? Costs double.
Good to see you on the roll, blade.
We march before dawn, captain.
We've been paid to bring in people like you.
You have the look of a soldier.
Old wounds ache worst in this wet.
Good to see you, comrade.
We drink tonight. Pull up a bench.
I have killed better than you. Leave.
Hunter? You walk like prey.
Night hunt. Stay behind me, hunter.
Is the kill shared with you yet, hunter?
A wamasu was seen near the village.
Poacher. Go. The others know of you.
Watch your step here, outsider.
The path is hard to see after dark.
Many here know your face, outsider.
The moon is thin. Hunting weather, outsider.
Leave the dead water, cutpurse.
You lost? This door is not for you.
Dry feet. Talk quiet, reed.
The fence crew wants a word, reed.
Work for you tonight, if you want it.
You talked, water-rat. Expect a cold swim.
All things turn, seeker. What brings you?
The temple is open at night as well.
The priests asked after you, seeker.
The third sermon starts soon, seeker.
All things turn. The temple doors do not.
Passenger fares are paid at the plank.
No boats leave till dawn.
Fair tide. Your berth is clear, pilot.
Need a crossing? I'll wake the pilot.
Off the boat. Off the dock.
The tree has no sap up this season.
A sap-speaker is asleep in there.
Be welcome among the roots, friend of the roots.
The sap-speakers are inside, friend of the roots.
We want no trouble from you, Reed-walker.
State your purpose, traveller.
The way is shut until morning.
Did you hold to the marked path, traveller?
The markers are fresh-cut, traveller.
You cut a marker. Leave this way.
Who asked you aboard, then?
Teeth out. Who's there?
Good haul this month, mate. You'll see your cut.
Your share's on the barrel, mate.
Over the side with you, landsman.
Why are you watching me?
Why are you out at night?
Early for your lessons, young one?
Your lessons begin at moonrise, young one.
We know about your hands. Keep them still.
Visitors stare. Please do not.
Our lamps stay lit all night.
The array readings are good, neighbour.
We rest little here, neighbour.
Every one of us has heard what you did.
An offering has come to us.
An offering, after dark. The fire is lit.
The fire has been fed well, offering.
The Razor Prince knows your work, offering.
Kneel and bare your throat, offering.
Ask anything. Nothing leaves the shelves.
Must it be now, reader?
Your shelf is untouched, reader.
The lamp is lit, reader.
Grave-robber. That book stays.
Your licence, if you would.
The First Adjunct is in conference.
Attendance noted. All is in order, attendant.
Shut the door behind you, attendant.
Your conduct goes to the Grand Council.
Come about the fields, grower?
We're counting sacks. Mind the scales.
The first saltrice is cut, grower.
Rice again tonight, grower.
Get off our fields before I call the crew.
Your purse, soft-skin. Quickly.
Teeth in the grass. Keep moving.
Back again, soft-skin? Then sit.
The fire is small, but warm.
Wardens know our camp now, soft-skin.
Are you here for the names on the wall?
The vigil lasts all night, witness.
Thank you for coming, witness.
A candle is lit for you, witness.
You did that in our hall, in front of the names.
Root-sibling, or Warden spy?
The Veiled Reed take people at night, root-sibling.
By the unbound root, root-sibling.
Get inside, root-sibling. I'll bar the door.
Everyone here knows your face, informer.
No names, please. Not here.
Under the reed, friend. Speak softly.
Useful work lately, friend.
Night work suits you, friend.
You were never here. Understood?
Reed-folk? What brings you onto our stone?
Wandering at night? What is your road?
The tree at Vakka-Bur has sap running, stone-kin.
The fire is ours, stone-kin.
Hands off our stone, Reed-folk.
State your business. Briefly.
I am working. Be brief.
Ah, it is you. Acceptable.
You may speak, since you are here.
Your hands stay where I can see them.
Did the holder send you?
My work is done. Speak, then.
The debtors talk of your kindness.
By my home tree, you are out at this hour?
Please. Do not tell the holder.
Have you an appointment?
The office is shut, but I am still here.
Ah. Welcome. I mean that, I think.
The last of the accounts. Please, sit.
I have written your description down.
Need a boat? The post has three.
We load at night. The ropes are out.
Good water today. Where are you bound?
What do you need? The tide is turning.
The factor's men are coming. Go, quickly.
Ojel. A walker from another egg comes.
The tribe rests. Walk softly here.
Good day to come, ojel. The tide is out.
I extend the claw of greeting, ojel.
Hist piss. What you took is not yours.
What's it to be, Longshanks?
Who's that? Oh, it's you.
Longshanks! Back from the deep marsh?
The frogs won't shut up. Sit if you like.
That's going in the tally, Longshanks.
Good day. Is there something I might do?
It's dark, but perhaps I can spare a moment.
This house remembers your help, my friend.
Come in from the doorway, if you would.
I'll put a ward on you, I promise.
Address me as serjo.
Speak quickly. My master sleeps.
You have served the House well.
Sera, you may approach.
Workers who run are brought back.
What do you want?
It is dark for callers from the road.
My door is open to you, sera.
Closing the books. Make it quick.
I won't shout. I know your face now.
Is there a decent inn in this place?
The insects are loud again, every night.
Sera. You're more civil than most here.
What now? My boxes are still open.
I know people on the Tear road.
Halt. Name and business, friend.
Second watch. You're out late for the post.
You're always welcome at the post.
The brazier's warm till the roll is called.
Hand it over, or the serjeant hears of this.
My mill's by the sluice. Want something?
By Akatosh, I've only just shut the mill.
I'd hoped you'd come. The flour's good this week.
Lock the door behind you, would you?
There is the thief from the mill.
Do you know a dry road east?
It's too hot to sleep in this.
A letter from home came today.
I've a broken cart wheel to mend.
Take it. I've nothing worth a fight.
Walker has coin? I have goods.
The caravan leaves at first light. I am packing.
I kept the good rope for you, friend.
The lease is due. Buy something, friend?
This one will say nothing. Go, walker.
What does the walker want?
Another toll at the crossing. This one is nearly broke.
Walker pays well. This one remembers.
The moons are bright. Talk with this one.
This one is leaving. Now.
Blade oiled? The damp'll rust one in a week.
Forge is banked. What's wanted?
Hold this while I quench it, will you?
There's mead on the bench if you're staying.
Shor's bones. Put it back.
This swamp. I hate this swamp.
Pay's late. Third month running.
Fancy a sparring bout? Fair fight.
Pirates pay better than the Charter.
Do that again and you'll lose the hand.
Speak plainly, customer. I am busy.
The iron came late. The forge stays hot.
The blade is ready. Good work, that.
Pump the bellows if you are staying.
No excuses. Out of my forge.
Is the ferry running today?
Quiet night so far, friend.
You're a sight. What d'you need?
Grandfather's sword. Want to see it?
I don't want trouble. You'd best go.
Tar's still wet. Watch your feet.
Caulking by lamplight. She'll launch tomorrow.
Come and look at this hull!
There's a wreck down the coast, I hear.
Get off my slipway, hull-robber.
